# ABC

> ABC is an agentic business console on Arc. An AI agent with its own wallet launches a token, raises USDC, and runs business spending while an operator supervises through an audit-ledger interface.

**Status:** testnet on arc-testnet · **Hackathon:** Tameion Agents Hackathon · Canteen × Circle — AI x DeFi · **Built during hackathon:** Hook v2, Arc testnet deployment, executor, console, agent loop, and showcase site. v1 LGE hook and frontend existed before 27 Sep. · **Prior work:** Uniswap v4 LGE hook + manager and participant UI, with ETH deposits, a single swap window, and no fee split.

## Rubric map
C3 maps to "Agentic sophistication". C1 maps to "Circle tool usage". C2 maps to "Innovation". Novelty is C3 only.

## Scope of claims
- No users, partners, or metrics exist beyond those listed in this file.
- Everything under "Not built" is unshipped; there is no roadmap commitment in this file.
- Named projects are integrations or mentions, not partnerships, unless marked "partner" with a link.
- AI components are listed separately from deterministic code; mocked model calls are marked "mocked".

- **Run it (in CI):** `forge test`

## What shipped
- **Live:** LGEHook v2 on Arc testnet with USDC deposits and 25/50/25 fee split; LGEManager factory for per-agent launches; Executor pipeline with Circle SCA signer; Operator console (Vite + React + wagmi)
- **Prototype:** Agent LLM loop with signed rationales; Showcase-site architecture
- **Mocked:** None
- **Not built:** Mainnet deployment; Public hosted console; Inference x402 rail

## How it works
Operator instructs agent → agent proposes typed intent → pipeline quotes, simulates, checks policy → agent wallet signs → transaction broadcasts → ledger records final state.
- **Onchain:** LGEHook v2 runs the token sale, pools USDC, custodies LP, splits swap fees, and locks LP when booked participant fees reach the raise size.
- **Offchain:** Executor Hono API + pg-boss worker maintains intent state machine and Circle wallet signing.
- **AI/agent:** LLM chooses intents and writes rationales; it cannot sign or exceed policy limits.
- **Deterministic code:** Policy checks, quote math, limit enforcement, and onchain execution are deterministic code.

## Novelty
- **New:** A single console gives an agent a real wallet, token launch, and business-spending controls, with every intent ledgered and policy-enforced before signing. (C3)
- **Not new:** Uniswap v4 hooks, ERC-20 tokens, developer-controlled wallets, intent pipelines.
- **Why the combination matters:** Most agent tools move money without limits or are chat-only copilots. ABC binds model judgment to contract-enforced budgets and a ledger.

## Limits
- Console runs locally; no public hosted URL yet.
- All deployments are Arc testnet.
- Inference nanopayment rail is architected but not fully wired.
- One live token per agent is enforced; a failed launch can be retried only with a new token.
- **Dependencies:** Arc testnet RPC, Uniswap v4 Arc deployment, Circle wallets, Anthropic API, Postgres.
